facts.text: Chackbay was founded in the early 20th century as a farming community, its name coming from the Chacahoula Native American tribe that once lived there.
The town sits along Bayou Lafourche and is surrounded by bayous and marshes, making fishing and outdoor adventures a local favorite.
Chackbay lies on the northern edge of Lafourche Parish at roughly 29°53′9″N 90°47′27″W, placing it just north of the parish line.
Settlement in Chackbay follows the main roads, which run on higher ground, while the areas away from roads remain wetland and largely undeveloped.
Chackbay is part of the Houma–Bayou Cane–Thibodaux metropolitan statistical area, linking it to the larger regional economy.
Chackbay’s residents celebrate Cajun traditions, with local festivals and cuisine reflecting the region’s rich cultural heritage.
